connector: Lucy and Edmund are back, and this time Edmund has been to Narnia too. Will he tell the truth? In Chapter 5, watch the choice he makes when Peter asks him, and what it costs Lucy.

a.raw: edmund gave lucy a superior look but he said nothing kind
a.fixed: Edmund gave Lucy a superior look, but he said nothing kind.
a.why: Edmund and Lucy are names. A comma goes before but, because it joins two complete thoughts. Gave and said are both past tense.

b.raw: peter went to the professor and he told him the whole story
b.fixed: Peter went to the Professor, and he told him the whole story.
b.why: Peter is a name, and the Professor is used as his name. A comma goes before and. Went and told are both past tense.

match.enchanted: Enchanted is about magic. Look for the meaning with a spell.
match.dominions: Dominions are places. Look for the meaning about lands.
match.wretched: Wretched is a feeling. Look for the unhappy meaning.
match.treachery: Treachery is about trust. Look for the meaning about betraying someone.

cards.title: World Notes: Old Country Houses
cards.sub: A real thing behind the story
cards.todo: Read the note. Then read the chapter with your lens in mind.
text: The Professor's house is a big, old country house. In England, some very old houses are so famous that people come to see them.
In Chapter 5, the housekeeper, Mrs. Macready, shows groups of visitors around the house.
That is why the children have to hide when the visitors come, and why they end up in the wardrobe!

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it's Opti. Edmund has been to Narnia too. Will he tell the truth? Watch his choice in Chapter 5.
transcripts.guide1: Word work: match form words, fix verbs that slip, and hear the beats.
transcripts.guide2: Read Chapter 5. Then try my video in Read Like a Writer.
transcripts.guide3: Today you make the link between a choice and what it causes clearer.

notes.wordParts: The root form means shape. uniform = one shape for everyone. transform = to change shape.
notes.grammar: Keep your verbs in the same time. If a story starts in the past (walked, ate), every verb stays in the past.
notes.spelling: Every beat in a word has one vowel sound. Count the sounds, not the letters: de-tail has two beats.
notes.wgrd: A choice can cost someone else. Edmund's lie made Lucy look like she was not telling the truth.
vocab: betraying someone's trust in a serious way

plate.alt: A painting of a green park with cows, a lake with swans and a boat, and a large country house far back among the trees
plate.credit: Wivenhoe Park, Essex · John Constable, 1816 · National Gallery of Art, Washington · Public domain
plate.look: A painting by John Constable of a real country house in England, in 1816. The house stands far back across the park, with a lake, swans and cows in front. Big old houses like this had so many rooms that visitors came to see them, just like the Professor's house in Chapter 5.

mods.todo: Listen to Opti. Then tap the lens you will use today.
mods.script: [warmly] Here's today's reading tip. A choice can cost someone else. Watch what Edmund says when Peter asks him about Narnia, and who pays for it. Then tap one of the two lenses below to use while you read. You don't need to write anything.

mods.todo: Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or B and type it the right way.
mods.script: Let's fix a sentence. The correct one first. Edmund had been to Narnia, but he told Peter and Susan it was only a game. Been and told both point to the past, so the sentence never slips. Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or Sentence B, and type it the right way.

mods.todo: Read the poem out loud. Then answer the question.
mods.script: [curious] Here's a poem by Robert Louis Stevenson. Read it out loud. Who is riding by, all night long, in the dark and wet? You never see him. Then answer the question.

mods.todo: Tap a word, then tap what it means. Match all four words.
mods.script: Watch one match first. Find form, and remember: it means shape. Formless. Form, plus less, without. Formless means without a shape, like a cloud of fog. That's my match! Read the Remember box. Then tap a word, and tap what it means. Match all four words.

mods.todo: Tap a word, then tap its meaning. Match all four words.
mods.script: Here's a strong word from Chapter 5. Beastly. Peter says Edmund has been perfectly beastly to Lu. Acting like a beast? Very mean! Now tap a word, then tap its meaning. Match all four.

mods.todo: Find the verb that slipped. Tap Now check your thinking. Then tap every word that is wrong.
mods.script: Which verb slipped? Susan looked inside and sees only coats. Looked is past. Sees is now. Sees slipped! It should be saw. Find the slipped verb in each sentence, and tap Now check your thinking. Then fix the paragraph.

mods.todo: Read the rule. In each row, tap the word that matches.
mods.script: Beat detective time! Which word has two beats? Wardrobe. Lamp. Enchanted. Clap them. Ward, robe: two! Lamp: one. En, chant, ed: three. Wardrobe it is. Read the rule. Then in each row, tap the one word that matches.

mods.todo: Read Chapter 5 in your book. Then try the Truth Watch below.
mods.script: Read Chapter 5 in your book, with your lens in mind. Then try the Truth Watch, and watch my video in the Read Like a Writer box before you write.

mods.label: Opti shows you how
mods.script: [warmly] Let's try all three parts with a different sentence from Chapter 5. Edmund, who was becoming a nastier person every minute, thought that he had scored a great success. Part one, read like a reader. Edmund thinks he won, but he hurt Lucy. Part two, read like a writer. Lewis tucks a fact about Edmund into the middle, with who. Part three, mimic. Here's mine: Opti, who was getting sleepier every minute, thought that one more chapter would do. Now it's your turn with the sentence about Edmund being tired. Write one sentence in each box.

mods.todo: Answer each question in full sentences. Use details from the book.
mods.script: Three questions, in full sentences. One, what Edmund says, and what it does to Lucy. Two, how Peter answers him. Three, the Professor's main argument about Lucy's story.

mods.todo: Add one connecting word, like because or as a result.
mods.script: Today you make the link clearer. Clara's draft was three short sentences. Her revision joins the choice to what it causes, with words like because. Add one connecting word to your paragraph.

virtue.name: honesty
virtue.title: Truth Watch: Is someone being honest?

items.t: Edmund says he and Lucy were only pretending.
items.why: That was a lie. He had been to Narnia too.

items.t: Peter and Susan tell the Professor the whole story.
items.why: They are honest about what has been happening.

items.t: Peter says that, until now, he would always have said Lucy was the more truthful one.
items.why: He tells the truth about Lucy, even after an argument.
